thread:
IncidentBot: 🔔 ALERT: elevated 5xx rate detected on streaming-gateway-prod (us-west-2). 5xx jump to ~7% over last 2m, primarily 502 / 504. Trigger: streaming-gateway/5xx-threshold. Paging oncall.

Alex: ack — i'm oncall, seeing the alert. digging in.

Sam: +1, checking dashboards now. any customer-facing pages yet?

SupportBot: CustomerImpact: ~120 connections experiencing disconnects; a few API customers reported aborted streams. CS notified a small set (customer-A, customer-C).

Maria: I'm pulling gateway logs and tailing router metrics. preliminary looks like a surge of chunked-encoding errors + upstream connection resets.

Alex: running quick pod check 
```
Alex: kubectl get pods -n prod-streaming | grep gateway
NAME                                        READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
streaming-gateway-5bb8f7d6f7-ptz4q         2/2     Running   0          3d
streaming-gateway-5bb8f7d6f7-qk2lm         1/2     CrashLoop 3          4h
streaming-gateway-5bb8f7d6f7-r8j2p         2/2     Running   0          3d

Alex: one replica is crashlooping, likely the culprit for increased error surface.
```

Jen: logs show repeated `write: connection reset by peer` when proxying to model-backend. snippet:
```
Jen: 2026-06-10T12:03:21Z ERROR proxy upstream write failed: write tcp 10.20.7.9:443->10.21.3.4:51234: write: connection reset by peer
Jen: 2026-06-10T12:03:22Z WARN streaming chunk write failed: broken pipe
```

Ravi: I see an increase in client cancellations in the telemetry (code: client.cancelled) — lots of short-lived streams from mobile sdk v0.9.4. Could be a client-side retry loop + server backpressure dance.

Sam: rolling a quick healthcheck dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.example/org/streaming-gateway?from=now-30m (please open)

Alex: quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase gateway replica count 2) enable aggressive request throttling for long-lived streams 3) route traffic away from the crashlooping pod by cordon/drain 4) fallback to non-stream variant for affected customers. Thoughts?

Maria: agree. immediate: cordon the crashloop pod and scale to +2 replicas. also bump upstream timeouts to avoid mid-stream resets while we debug.

Alex: doing cordon and scale now.
```
Alex: kubectl cordon streaming-gateway-5bb8f7d6f7-qk2lm -n prod-streaming
Alex: kubectl delete pod streaming-gateway-5bb8f7d6f7-qk2lm -n prod-streaming
Alex: kubectl scale deployment streaming-gateway -n prod-streaming --replicas=5
```

Alex: scaled. new pods coming up. monitoring.

DeployBot: Deploy event: rolling restart of streaming-gateway triggered by Alex (reason: live mitigation). CI checks passed.

Jen: after scale i still see some 502s but overall error rate falling from 7% → 2.1% in 5m. looks promising.

Ravi: I pushed a short-lived routing rule to reduce long-lived streams to max 5 concurrent per client IP to reduce resource contention. Applied as temporary rule.

Sam: added a gateway-level soft-rate-limit for chunked-encoding streams (60s initial credit) — should reduce retry storms.

Maria: logs show the crashlooping pod had OOMs right before restart. stack traces point to a non-blocking flush path hitting a mem spike when many clients cancel mid-stream. snippet:
```
Maria: runtime: out of memory: cannot allocate 4194304 bytes
Maria: goroutine 123 [running]:
Maria: net/http.(*chunkedWriter).Write(0xc000...)
```

Alex: OOM => good catch. We should enable smaller chunk buffer + protect against client-initiated cancellations leaking buffers. create ticket to investigate memory path.

Jen: for immediate customer mitigation, Sam can we set routing fallback for top 5 affected customers to polling/non-stream endpoint?

Sam: yes, pushed route override for customer-A and customer-C to polling endpoints and notified support.

SupportBot: Notified customers: customer-A (ops@customer-a.com), customer-C (support@customer-c.com). Providing ETA: 30m.

Alex: monitoring shows continued downward trend. current 5xx ~0.9% last 2m. latency for streaming requests back to baseline.

Ravi: creating follow-up ticket for memory leak / chunked writer path. assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml to review model-backend connection handling.

Alex: filing post-incident items now. I'll keep thread updated with RCA pointers.

Maria: quick note — client SDK v0.9.4 has aggressive reconnect on aborts; engineering to coordinate with SDK team for backoff change.

Jen: verification: ran end-to-end smoke for streamed completions. sample command:
```
Jen: curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","prompt":"hi"}'
```
Jen: stream remained stable for 2m in our smoke tests.
```

Alex: summary: cause = memory pressure on streaming-gateway pod during high client cancellations causing OOM/crashloop → upstream resets → 5xx spike. mitigation = cordon + restart crashloop pod, scale replicas, apply soft throttles and per-client concurrency limits, route critical customers to polling fallback. impact = limited subset customers saw disconnects, no data loss, estimated ~120 active connections affected. next steps = RCA ticket, SDK backoff tweak, improve chunked writer memory caps, add alert for pod OOM bursts.

Sam: marking as mitigated. logging final metrics to incident tracker.

Alex: handing off to oncall-next (Maria) for the 1hr watch window. thanks everyone. :tada:

IncidentBot: Incident resolved? status changed to mitigated by Alex.

Maria: watching — will escalate if error rate rises above 2% again.

SupportBot: Follow-up sent to customers with mitigation details and next steps.

Alex: creating the RCA doc now: https://docs.redwood.example/incidents/1950009999-rca (placeholder).

Jen: +1 — good work team.
